Hi Gina — thanks for the clear list. I pulled together a short summary and an initial playbook for your legal/compliance review (attached). High level answers below, and I've looped in Laura (AM) to coordinate procurement timing.

1) Region pinning: Confirmed. For Dedicated deployments we offer region pinning per-tenant. By default we provision all compute, KV cache, and persistent storage in the customer-selected region (eu-central-1). Cross-region replication is opt-in and disabled for your account unless explicitly requested and authorized via a separate change request.

2) Isolation: Dedicated includes tenant-level VPCs and isolated block storage. Host OS and hypervisor-level metadata are not exposed between tenants. We do collect aggregated metrics for platform health but these are scrubbed of tenant-identifying metadata.

3) Deletion SLA: Standard deletion path: live store (primary) deletion: 24–72 hours; cache eviction (KV/prefix caches): within 24 hours after request completion; backup removal: depends on retention window — backups created before deletion request are scheduled for secure purge within 30 days unless you elect expedited removal. We can offer a tighter SLA (7 days for backups) as a contractual addendum for Dedicated customers. We provide deletion attestations (PDF) and can include a signed, timestamped audit entry referencing the purge operation.

4) Retention controls: Tenant admins can set retention windows per workspace. We also support retention-lock (immutable retention) only by explicit configuration during onboarding and with a documented change control process.

I'm attaching: Dedicated_Residency_SLA_v1.pdf (summary + attestations process), data-deletion-playbook.docx (step-by-step), and a region diagram.

Next steps:
- Laura will send an estimated timeline and contract language for the backup-acceleration SLA option.
- I recommend a 30-minute call with Stephanie (security) and one of our infra engineers to walk through the purging flow and attestation proof. Are you available next Tue/Wed?

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec — Redwood Inference

Hi all — Steph from Security here. Quick technical clarifications below; I'll join the call if helpful.

- Host logs: we redact tenant IDs from kernel and hypervisor logs by default. Application-layer request IDs are tenant-scoped and stored only within the tenant's region unless cross-region replication is enabled. For forensic requests we can provide scoped logs under an NDA and only via a secure transfer.

- Attestation contents: our deletion attestations include: tenant name, operation id, ISO8601 timestamp, list of purged object identifiers (object IDs + path), hash summaries (SHA-256) for each object pre- and post- purge, operator id (system or service account), and a signed PGP block from our ops team. We can provide a redacted sample attestation; see the attached sample page from the playbook.

- Backup manifest: the purge job emits a manifest file listing snapshot IDs, creation timestamps, and a status for each snapshot. For standard purge we publish the manifest to a secure S3 location (eu-central-1) and notify the tenant admin when the purge completes. For expedited purges we also provide an audit log entry and a signed attestation.

I'm attaching a single-page sample excerpt from our playbook for reference (embedded in the PDF we sent earlier).

—Stephanie
Security Engineering Manager, Redwood Inference
